kubernetes.description: The kubernetes manager ships no default file pattern, so image tags hardcoded inside a chart's templates/ are invisible to Renovate while the same chart's values.yaml pins are bumped. Scoped to templates/ so the vendored upstream CRDs under crds/ -- whose JSON schemas contain `image:` property names, not image references -- stay out of scope.

packageRules.description: The monitor image is keyed by FDB minor version in the operator initContainers map -- each entry copies libfdb_c_<key>.so, so the tag must stay on that minor. Renovate sees three occurrences of one repository and bumps them all to latest, which breaks the init container. Bump these by hand alongside fdb.version.

Crossplane's version is pinned twice -- the xp-mp chart's dependency, and the helm Release the installation composition installs onto the management cluster -- and scripts/check-versions.sh holds the two equal. They also have to agree across the handover, where a composite created by the boot plane's Crossplane is adopted by the management plane's, so a bump is a decision about both planes at once rather than about one file. A control-plane upgrade has to be reconciled against the provider and function packages it runs, which Renovate bumps separately and which do not move in lockstep with it. Bump by hand, both copies in one change.

The Keycloak Operator is expected to run the same version as the Keycloak it manages, and the two are pinned in different files -- the instance in queenswood-keycloak's values.yaml, the operator in the keycloak-operator chart's vendored templates/operator.yaml. Group them so they move in one PR. That PR only rewrites the operator's image tag: the chart is a vendored copy of upstream's kubernetes.yml, so its ClusterRoles and the CRDs under crds/ must be re-vendored from the matching release tag in the same change, and both Chart.yaml appVersions updated.
